questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'From Kingdom to Empire' refers to.
questions.a: An empire joins many kingdoms and peoples under one ruler; the Mauryan empire, built from Magadha, was the first to stitch most of the subcontinent into one political fabric.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'From Kingdom to Empire'.
questions.a: An empire is scale: what a king does for one land, an emperor must do for many lands at once.

questions.q: Under which section is 'From Kingdom to Empire' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Chandragupta Maurya and Kautilya' refers to.
questions.a: Chandragupta Maurya, guided by the minister Kautilya, overthrew the Nandas and built the Mauryan empire; the Arthashastra, attributed to Kautilya, remains a manual of statecraft from that age.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Chandragupta Maurya and Kautilya'.
questions.a: A ruler and a strategist together: the throne of Magadha plus the science of governance made an empire.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Chandragupta Maurya and Kautilya' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Ashoka and the Kalinga War' refers to.
questions.a: Ashoka's victorious Kalinga war filled him with remorse at the suffering of war; he turned to dhamma, righteous conduct, and spread his message through edicts carved on rocks and pillars across the empire.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Ashoka and the Kalinga War'.
questions.a: The mightiest conqueror became the preacher of peace: Ashoka measured greatness in welfare, not in victories.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Ashoka and the Kalinga War' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Running an Empire: Administration' refers to.
questions.a: The empire ran through provinces and districts, graded officials, spies and a standing army, taxes on land and trade, and roads and rest houses that bound distant parts to the capital at Pataliputra.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Running an Empire: Administration'.
questions.a: Administration is the empire's skeleton: officials, taxes and roads carried the ruler's word to the villages.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Running an Empire: Administration' taught, and from which source text?
